Subject: Redwood / HealthSync — post-call recap and proposed next steps

Thanks again for the time this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum.

Key items we heard on the call:
- You need request/response logging for observability, but any payloads that include PII must be redacted prior to storage.
- Headers and trace IDs are also considered sensitive by your security team; they prefer pseudonymization (non-reversible) and a 90-day retention cap for any telemetry derived from production traffic.
- Data residency: logs must remain in the US region for PHI-adjacent workloads.

Proposed actions (suggested owners & timeline):
1) Redwood to share a short PoC outline showing how we can redact request/response bodies and hash trace IDs (attachment: redwood-poc-outline.pdf) — due: 7/24 — owner: me.
2) Security evidence: send a checklist of what we can provide (SOC 2 artifacts, config examples, scrubbed sample logs) — owner: Rishi — due: 7/25.
3) Pilot kickoff: 2-week pilot once PoC scope agreed; pilot will include sample traffic and verification that redaction meets your acceptance criteria — target start: week of 7/31.

Questions we have for your team to confirm before the PoC:
- Can you confirm the exact headers you need redacted vs. allowed for routing (e.g., Authorization vs. X-Request-ID)?
- For trace IDs, do you prefer a deterministic hash map (same trace => same pseudonym) or a one-way hash per ingestion?
- Any legal/regulatory notes for retention shorter than 90 days?

Attachments: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (PoC scope), security-evidence-checklist.xlsx (placeholder — more items to follow).

If that looks good, I’ll schedule a short follow-up next Tuesday to lock scope.

Thanks,

Thanks Monica — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Headers: we absolutely need Authorization redacted. X-Request-ID and X-Trace-ID are used by our ops team to correlate flows; we’d prefer to keep those but pseudonymized (so they are consistent across the same trace). Is deterministic hashing feasible?

2) Request/response bodies: we have a set of endpoints that occasionally bubble up SSNs or full names. The acceptance criteria will be: no unredacted SSNs in persisted logs, and a redaction annotation in the log indicating the rule that triggered the mask (for audit). Can Redwood emit a sanitized sample we can review before the pilot?

3) Residency: US-only for now; any storage in eu/apac is a blocker.

Happy to join a short scope call next Tue.

—Ken

- Redaction metadata: Redwood can emit a standardized annotation (rule_id and redaction_type) alongside the sanitized entry so auditors can see why a value was masked.
- Residency: we’ll ensure any persisted logs for this pilot point to our US region; configs will be explicit in the PoC doc.

Subject: Re: Redwood / HealthSync — technical samples and evidence

Hi all — quick technical notes and an example.

1) Trace ID pseudonymization (recommended):
- Approach: keyed HMAC-SHA256 truncated to 16 hex chars. Deterministic per-tenant key; non-reversible without key.
- Pros: keeps same trace correlatable, low collision risk, no plaintext stored.
- Cons: requires key management (we can integrate with your KMS or use Redwood KMS per the Private offering).

2) Redaction annotation: we recommend a small metadata block appended to the log: {rule_id: "PII-NUM-01", redaction: "ssn_masked"} — sample below.

3) Retention: for the pilot we propose a default TTL of 90 days for sanitized logs. If you need shorter (30/7 days) we can parameterize per-route.

Sample (redacted) log line (COLLECTOR -> STORAGE):
2028-07-20T16:00:12Z INFO request completed method=POST path=/patients/create status=200 latency_ms=112 trace_pseudonym=9f7a3b2c4d6e1f0a user_id=acct-452 action=patient_create body={"name":"REDACTED","ssn":"REDACTED","notes":"masked"} redaction_metadata="rule_id=PII-NUM-01;redaction_type=regex_mask"

I attached a preliminary security evidence checklist (security-evidence-checklist.xlsx) with items we can provide: SOC 2 scoping, sample scrubbed logs, config snippets for retention and KMS integration, and a list of cryptographic libraries used for hashing. Priyom and I can assemble the sanitized sample logs for your review by 7/25.

—Rishi
